data.narrative:
Cohesive Robotics is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by David Pietrocola that has raised $5M+. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine private robotics companies and one public comparable (ticker 277810.KQ), though the peer set remains sparse for seed-stage companies in this sector.

Stage-progression methodology was the sole applicable triangulation method. Using the $5M total raised as a proxy for entry valuation and applying a standard 2.5x multiplier for progression from seed to the next stage yields an implied valuation of $12M. Peer-median analysis was inapplicable due to insufficient datapoints; while eight same-sector peers exist (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Bedrock Robotics), fewer than three met the filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier comparability, making a narrow peer median unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $11M to $14M, with a median point of $12M. This estimate carries material uncertainty given the single-method foundation and limited seed-stage peer comparables in robotics. Key risks to this range include founder track record depth, technology differentiation within the crowded robotics space, and market adoption timelines—factors not fully captured by stage-based progression alone. A more refined valuation would require either expanding the comparable set or obtaining additional operational metrics from Cohesive Robotics.
